profile.campus: Secaucus / North Bergen, Hudson County, New Jersey (Equinix New York metro campus)
profile.reading:
Equinix's own facility page places this building, NY3, at 600 Jefferson Avenue in Secaucus, New Jersey 07094, describing a two story, reinforced concrete structure of 250,853 square feet, the largest of Equinix's Secaucus buildings by floor area. Published specifications list N+1 generator redundancy, 240v/415v power distribution, N+2 cooling redundancy described as suited to high density and AI workloads, and a minimum cabinet density of 8kVA, higher than the other Secaucus buildings in this registry. UPS redundancy is not disclosed on the page. Security is listed as 24/7 with biometric access, fire suppression uses a double interlock pre action system, and Equinix advertises a 99.9999 percent plus global uptime guarantee. The page highlights direct fiber access into New York carrier hotel ecosystems and lists Internet Exchange, Internet Access, Metro Connect, Fiber Connect, and Cross Connect services, along with certifications including ISO 22301, ISO 27001, ISO 9001, PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type II, and SOC 2 Type II. No megawatt capacity figure and no year of construction are published for the existing building.

Data Center Frontier, a trade publication, separately reported in 2026 on a further NY3 expansion project underway, targeting roughly 300,000 additional square feet with a first phase of about 1,200 colocation cabinets, designed for an average power density of 9 to 10 kW per cabinet, well above the roughly 5kW average the article attributed to the existing Secaucus campus. That expansion is a distinct construction project from the currently operating NY3 building described above and this registry has not confirmed a completion date.

NY3 sits inside a cluster of Equinix buildings, NY2 through NY6, addressed within roughly a mile of each other around Secaucus in Hudson County. The same Data Center Frontier reporting described Equinix's wider New York and New Jersey metro area as nine IBX buildings totaling about 739,000 square feet of technical space, and detailed a neighboring building, NY5, built in 2012 and expanded in 2016 to 20 megawatts of critical power capacity with four utility feeder lines and eight 2.5 megawatt generators, a campus that stayed online through a full week without grid power during Superstorm Sandy in 2012. That 20 megawatt figure belongs to NY5, not NY3.

Equinix was founded in 1998 by Al Avery and Jay Adelson and has grown into a global colocation and interconnection company running more than 260 IBX data centers across more than 70 metro areas, converting to a real estate investment trust in 2015. Hudson County's Equinix cluster sits roughly ten miles from Lower Manhattan, shaped by lower New Jersey real estate costs and proximity to the Wall Street financial corridor.
profile.campus_sqft: Published individual square footage for four of the five Secaucus buildings totals 550,057 sq ft (NY2 131,040 + NY3 250,853 + NY4 151,771 + NY6 16,393 per Equinix's own site). NY5's individual square footage is not published by Equinix. The wider 9-site Equinix New York/New Jersey metro area totals roughly 739,000 sq ft of technical space per Data Center Frontier (2026).
profile.capacity_note: N+2 Cooling redundancy; UPS redundancy not published; no MW power capacity published
profile.facility_note: Per Equinix own site, this NY3 facility is located at 600 Jefferson Avenue, Secaucus, NJ 07094 and totals 250,853 sq ft. Redundancy: N+2 Cooling redundancy; UPS redundancy not published. No MW power capacity figure is published on this page.

profile.regional_context: Equinix describes NY3 (Secaucus) as its largest New York metro site, serving major financial, media, and enterprise companies with an Ad-IX advertising exchange and cloud on-ramps.
profile.campus_power_note: Equinix has not published a building specific megawatt figure for NY2, NY3, NY4, or NY6. The only building specific power figure publicly reported for the 5-building Secaucus campus is NY5's 20 MW of critical power capacity (built 2012, expanded 2016), per Data Center Frontier (2026). That figure belongs to NY5 only and should not be read onto any other building in this cluster.
profile.facility_type_note: Part of Equinix's New York metro campus. The New Jersey facilities in this registry (Hudson County, Middlesex County, North Bergen, Secaucus) correspond to Equinix's Secaucus campus (NY2-NY6), while NY1 (the historic 165 Halsey Street carrier hotel in Newark, also tied to a Tishman operator record elsewhere in this registry) and other NY-branded buildings (NY7, NY9, NY11, and upstate NY13 in Elmsford) complete the 10-facility metro per Equinix's own site.

reading.body:
Equinix NY3 occupies 250,853 square feet in Secaucus, New Jersey, as part of a nine-building metro campus in Hudson County. The facility's published specifications include N+2 cooling redundancy, but no megawatt power capacity figure is published by the operator. Without a disclosed power rating, the density of AI workloads this building can host cannot be calculated from available data.

The Secaucus campus sits 10 miles from Lower Manhattan and concentrates colocation space for financial trading, media, and enterprise companies seeking Wall Street proximity at lower real estate cost than Manhattan itself offers. The neighboring NY5 building, which published 20 megawatts of critical power capacity, demonstrated operational resilience during Superstorm Sandy in 2012 with four utility feeder lines and eight backup generators. Equinix describes NY3 as its largest New York metro site and operates Ad-IX, an advertising exchange, plus cloud on-ramps to AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle Cloud, and IBM Cloud from this facility.

New Jersey has 48 mapped data center facilities, of which only five operators publish megawatt figures, totaling 111.3 MW statewide. This campus's published capacity rank in the state is not established because Equinix has not published a megawatt figure for NY3. The absence of power disclosure limits assessment of whether this 250,000-square-foot facility represents significant AI infrastructure density or serves primarily as interconnection and colocation for financial services.
